newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Caja Madrid buys 3 pct of Telefonica. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spain's Caja Madrid buys 3 pct of Telefonica. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]

text.p: Spain's savings bank Caja de Madrid said it bought three percent of Telefonica de Espana for 102 billion pesetas and added that it does not rule out further purchases.

"(The group does not rule out) that it continues the purchase of shares in Spain's primary telecommunciations group," Caja de Madrid said in a statement. (Corrects to show statement was by Caja de Madrid, not Telefonica.)
With the purchase, Caja de Madrid owns 29 million shares in the group.
Caja de Madrid said Telefonica was attractive because of its diversification in markets and products and the rise in the number of lines.
It also pointed to strong development in mobile phones, the expansion of TISA in strong-growth areas, the new global alliance and a strong bet on the development of Multimedia projects.
In addition, the group's high cash-flow, good financial debt ratio, the maintenance of operating margins and the gradual reduction of extraordinary debt were financial reasons for the purchase.
Above all, Caja de Madrid pointed to Telefonica's expected profit growth of 15 percent on average a year for the next four years.
"The analysts of the Caja de Madrid also consider that the share has a clear potential to rise medium and long-term," it said.
